notes: v273 — NAV-TOP-CUTOFF-STILL + NAV-CARD-NO-USEFUL-INFO + NAV-SMALL-SCREEN-BLUE (owner verdict, Mon Oct 26, 2026 17:46 MDT, fresh native v57 install, drive home: 'All the issues with the GPS remain the same — the screen is still cutting off, the card is not giving any useful information, and when I make the screen small it's basically turning blue'). Reproduced under HIS conditions first: the recordings are 1080x2520 (Fold7 cover display, DPR 2.625), so the drive viewport is 411x960 CSS px and the system PiP window measures ~221x139 CSS px off his own frame — the earlier harnesses all used 768x1024. ITEM 1 (top cutoff): the v260 lift was a flat 0.49 x height tuned at 768x1024; the exact homography at 411x960 leaves the top uncovered at side headings (projected far reach ~593px against ~614px needed) and even at 768x1024 it fails in the corners at diagonal headings (v260 sampled only the straight-ahead reach). FIX: the lift is DERIVED per viewport — NAVPURE.coverageLiftPx finds the smallest translate whose inverse homography keeps the whole top strip inside the plane at every heading (coverage in the lift is a window, not a threshold: overshoot drags the far field across the perspective eye plane), and paintPlane feeds it the live clientWidth/clientHeight; the follow camera compensates off the same value, as before. ITEM 2 (card gives no useful information): the PiP bottom line (.nv-drive-pip-line) and the docked face's line (.bub-line) were white-space:nowrap + text-overflow:ellipsis — at PiP width the street name was cut mid-word by the CSS itself ('130 m · Turn right onto Herita…', his frame). Both lines now wrap whole words — the full distance + instruction, two lines at these widths; nothing ellipsizes. ITEM 3 (small screen blue): PiP enter/exit swapped the face but NOTHING re-fit the Leaflet map — no invalidateSize on the PiP seam and no window resize handler anywhere in the web code. The map kept its full-screen pixel size (plane ~1069x2880) inside the CSS-shrunk PiP plane (~575x417), so the map centre sat at (534,1440), outside the visible box: the window showed a stale-offset slice of map and, where the slice ran off the plane, the viewport's sky gradient (navy -> blue). FIX: refitDriveMap — invalidateSize + a drive tick, the exact pair the parked-restore path already trusts — runs on PiP enter AND exit through a hook the drive closure registers at map creation (S._refitDrive), and on debounced window resize while a drive is live (fold/unfold is the same defect on this phone). PROOF: new tools/nav-verdict-v273-test.js 23/23 — RED-first on the pre-fix tree (13 failures: both homography witnesses, no-refit on PiP enter/exit, both nowrap pins); geometry verified at 411x960, 768x1024, 360x640, 960x411 and the 221x139 PiP size. tools/nav-v260-test.js re-pinned for the derived lift (supersession recorded in its check). REGRESSIONS: full-sweep A/B against the v272 tree (194 suites) — the ONLY delta is the new suite; every other suite's summary and FAIL-line count is identical, including nav-v260 24/24 (the re-pin), nav-traffic-v262 21/21, nav-lane-inset-v264 32/32, auth-gate-v269 51/51, close-end-future-v270 59/59 and the fuel-history v272 suite 16/16. NAMED, NOT BUILT: (a) the v57 APK bundles web v234 — a fresh install drives on v234 until the OTA download + restart lands, part of why a reinstall day shows the old behaviour wholesale; refreshing the bundle is a native-release act. (b) 2D mode still carries no lift: at exact side headings on tall screens a sky band can still show at the top in 2D (v260 left 2D byte-identical on purpose) — growing the plane or lifting the flat view is his call. (c) The PiP drive zoom stays 18 (~80 m across) — the refit makes it the RIGHT 80 m under the arrow; a PiP-specific zoom is a design choice, not made here. ON-PHONE PROOF (owner's verdict): next drive — (1) heading east or west full-screen, the map reaches the very top of the glass, no navy band; (2) minimise mid-route: the small window shows the road you are actually on, under the arrow, in the big map's colours; (3) the small window's bottom line shows the whole street name across two lines — nothing cut mid-word.
